question: A 74-year-old man presents with complaints of sudden severe crushing retrosternal pain. The pain radiated to his left arm shortly after it began, and he was subsequently rushed to the emergency department for evaluation. His troponins and creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) were elevated. Unfortunately, the patient died within the next 2 hours and an autopsy was performed immediately. The gross examination of the heart will show?

options.opb: Red granulation tissue surrounding the infarction

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "74-year-old man with sudden severe crushing retrosternal pain" -> "pain radiated to left arm" -> "elevated troponins and CK-MB" -> "indicates myocardial infarction" -> "myocardial infarction leads to tissue necrosis" -> "necrotic tissue appears pale initially" -> "subsequent inflammatory response occurs" -> "inflammatory response includes neutrophil infiltration" -> "possible development of granulation tissue" -> "gross examination shows pallor of the infarcted tissue" -> 85%

analysis: The patient experienced sudden severe chest pain and elevated troponins and CK-MB, indicating an acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Given that the patient died within 2 hours of the onset of symptoms, the gross examination of the heart would likely show pallor of the infarcted tissue, as this is characteristic of early myocardial infarction. Neutrophils and granulation tissue would not be prominent at this early stage, and a scar would not yet have formed.
